constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic parameters reported for TPU Luvosint: tensile elastic modulus of 27 MPa, compressive elastic modulus of 20 MPa, Poisson's ratio of 0.45, and ultimate tensile elongation of 5.2
Material incompressibility and stiffness qualitatively assumed in discussion regarding geometric fold width limits
control_variables: Pressure cycling limits and hold durations (0 to 500 kPa ramp, 10 s hold per level)
Gripper geometric dimensions (housing outer diameter 100 mm, inner ring opening diameter 30 mm, height 22 mm)
Ring material (TPU Luvosint) and manufacturing process (selective laser sintering)
Insert material (PLA) and manufacturing process (fused deposition modeling)
Use of three previously unactuated grippers for each insert geometry
dependent_variables: Number of discrete folds formed on the inner ring wall
Deformation pattern and spatial location of folds
Repeatability of fold pattern formation across different prototype specimens
Stability and retention of the programmed fold pattern over repeated actuations (50 cycles)
Temporal stability of programmed deformation after a one-week rest period
Success or failure of deformation programming for a given insert geometry

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Soft pneumatic grippers commonly encounter industrial adoption hurdles due to limited durability, low gripping forces, and energy dissipation from material deformation.
Imprinting fold locations into a flexible ring actuator via mechanical constraints (star-shaped inserts) during an initial 500 kPa pressurization cycle enables programmable deformation.
Inserts featuring 4, 5, and 8 tips reliably produce 4, 5, and 8 discrete inward folds corresponding precisely to the unrestrained spaces between tips.
The programmed fold patterns remain stable without the insert during subsequent actuation, across 50 pressure cycles (0 to 500 kPa), and after a one-week rest period.
Attempting to program a 2-fold configuration using a two-tip insert failed, yielding four folds due to uncontrolled compressive stress and buckling in the large unconstrained ring segments.
Selective laser sintering of TPU powder (Luvosint) enables additive manufacturing of monolithic flexible ring actuators with internal air cavities without support structures.

experimental_setup: Vertically aligned gripper fixture monitored by a camera positioned to record the internal opening of the ring
Custom PLA star-shaped form inserts with 2, 4, 5, or 8 protruding tips fabricated via Prusa MK3S+ FDM 3D printer
Compressed air pressurization system supplying controlled pressure up to 500 kPa to the internal air channel
Selective laser sintering (EOS P-series) fabrication of the flexible ring from TPU Luvosint powder, cleaned with compressed air and ultrasonic vibration
PolyJet 3D printing (Keyence Agilista 3200) of the transparent urethane-based housing (AR-M2) for visual monitoring
Programming protocol: insert placement, pressurization to 500 kPa maintained for 60 s, depressurization, insert removal, and subsequent re-pressurization without the insert
Cyclic endurance test: 50 cycles ramping between 0 and 500 kPa with 10 s hold time per pressure state
Long-term retention test: re-evaluating fold pattern retention after a one-week rest period
future_work: Investigating automatic deformation programming by embedding artificial structural weaknesses or features directly into the ring during additive manufacturing
Testing whether an already programmed ring can be reprogrammed to a different fold count
Investigating alternative materials or optimized wall cross-sections to enable stable two-fold configurations
Determining the upper physical limit on fold count and identifying the material-specific minimum fold width based on ring circumference
independent_variables: Number of protruding tips on the geometric insert (2, 4, 5, or 8 tips)
Actuation state and presence of insert (programming phase with insert vs. operation phase without insert)
Actuation pressure magnitude and cycling (0 to 500 kPa)
Number of actuation cycles (up to 50 cycles)
Elapsed resting duration prior to re-actuation (immediate vs. 1 week later)
limitations_inferred: No quantitative gripping force, retention force, or payload measurements were performed to evaluate real grasping performance.
No physical grasping or manipulation tests with actual objects (e.g., pralines or cables) were conducted.
Testing was restricted to 50 actuation cycles and one week of resting, leaving long-term fatigue life, creep behavior, and durability over thousands of industrial cycles unknown.
No mathematical, kinematic, or finite element models were developed to predict stress fields, critical wrinkling thresholds, or deformation shapes.
Evaluation was confined to a single maximum pressure level (500 kPa) and a single TPU material formulation.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Inability to generate a stable two-fold pattern due to excessive compressive forces and spontaneous fold formation in unconstrained segments or insufficient material stiffness.
Existence of an anticipated upper limit on the achievable fold count governed by decreasing fold width, material stiffness, and incompressibility relative to ring circumference.
Shape programming via physical form inserts is an inherently manual process requiring manual insertion and removal.
Re-programmability of a previously programmed ring to a different fold configuration was not evaluated.
Soft grippers in general exhibit limited durability and low gripping forces in industrial environments due to material deformation losses.
main_results: Geometric inserts with 4, 5, and 8 tips successfully and repeatably programmed 4, 5, and 8 discrete inward folds into the flexible ring actuator.
Programmed fold patterns were fully retained upon subsequent pressurization to 500 kPa in the absence of the insert.
Programmed deformation patterns exhibited stability over 50 consecutive pressure cycles (0 to 500 kPa) and remained unchanged after a one-week rest period.
Two-fold programming failed, resulting in four folds (two folds per unrestrained half-ring) due to buckling under compressive stress.
The localized structural memory mechanism was shown to be viable using an additively manufactured TPU ring without embedded sensors or active multi-channel controls.
performance_metrics: Fold formation accuracy (correspondence between number of insert tips/unconstrained spaces and resulting folds)
Repeatability of fold patterns across three independent prototypes per geometry
Cycle durability (preservation of programmed fold shape across 50 pressure cycles)
Temporal shape retention (stability of fold pattern after a one-week rest interval)
possible_gap_implications: Manual insertion of programming molds creates a process bottleneck, indicating that practical industrial implementation will require automated or in-situ additive manufacturing feature integration.

Without empirical gripping force and payload characterization, it remains unverified whether shape pre-programming actually provides superior grasping efficiency or force delivery compared to standard ring grippers.
The failure of the 2-fold configuration points to a minimum constraint density required to prevent uncontrolled buckling in thin-walled elastomeric ring geometries.
The absence of mechanics-based predictive models means fold programming currently depends entirely on empirical trial-and-error rather than deterministic design guidelines.
paper.research_objective: To present the design and experimentally investigate the adaptability and shape-programmability of a pneumatically actuated, centrically closing soft multi-fold ring gripper whose deformation pattern (number and location of folds) is predetermined prior to deployment using geometric inserts during initial pressurization.
paper.research_problem: Industrial handling requires adaptable grippers, but conventional rigid grippers lack geometry flexibility while soft grippers often suffer from low gripping force, insufficient structural stiffness, limited durability, and energy dissipation during deformation; balancing initial shape conformity with adaptive compliance without complex external controls or embedded sensors remains a key challenge.
paper.title: Design and Experimental Validation of a Soft, Shape-Programmable Multi-fold Gripper
